note: Three Expert tunes by ear: one with two leaps of a 6th, sung with the tune and then over the chords alone; one that starts on Fa and has a dotted note, with the metronome; and one with two leaps of a 7th, alone and then a cappella. The tunes' notes are degree tokens, each stage names its button, and the old Key choice is moves (key any) with its line opening {{?key}}.

exercise.title: Tunes with awkward leaps and dotted notes
exercise.why: A wide leap lands in tune when you hear its landing note before you sing it, and a dotted note lands in time when you feel the beat it holds through, so each tune is heard first and sung second.

cells.text:
Press Play below to hear the tune: the mic starts with it. It opens with a leap of a 6th from {{1}} up to {{6}}, and its second bar leaps a 6th again, from {{3}} up to the high {{1}}. Listen once, then sing along. Sing it on "la".
Then press Tune below to mute the tune, and sing it over the chords alone.
Practice until both leaps land without a slide.
{{?key}}In another key the notes change, and both leaps are still a 6th.

This tune starts on {{4}}, not on {{1}}, and its second bar has a dotted note: {{5}} lasts a beat and a half, and a quick {{4}} follows it. Press Play below to hear the tune with the metronome: the mic starts with it. Sing along on "la".
If the quick {{4}} comes late, clap that bar with the metronome, then sing it again.

This tune has two leaps of a 7th: from the {{5}} under {{1}} up to {{4}} at the start, and from {{2}} up to the high {{1}} in the second bar. Press Play below to hear it alone, with no chords under it: the mic starts with it. Listen once, then sing along. Sing it on "la".
Then press Tune below to mute the tune, and sing it a cappella.
If a leap of a 7th misses, think of the octave and land one note under it.
